news.title: Morgan Stanley cut its riskiest reconciliation job in half — by making its agents less autonomous
news.summary_raw: Most enterprise AI deployments so far have focused on coding assistants and customer service bots. Morgan Stanley has deployed agents in one of banking's most accuracy-critical, deadline-driven workflows instead — profit and loss (P&L) reconciliation — and cut the work in half. The counterintuitive part: it got there by making the system less autonomous, not more.Humans stay tightly in the loop, and their decisions are iteratively turned into repeatable rules the system can apply on its
news.summary: Morgan Stanley reduced P&L reconciliation workload in half by using autonomous agents in tandem with human oversight. This approach involves iteratively turning human decisions into repeatable system rules, making the system less autonomous.
news.enterprise_use: Note this unique AI deployment approach, where humans and systems work together to create repeatable rules. This might be applied in specific areas where accuracy is critical, like account management or access control. JumpCloud and Freshservice might benefit from this collaboration-based approach in certain workflow contexts.

news.title: SkillOpt: Agent skills as trainable parameters
news.summary_raw:
AI agents often fail because their instructions, or skills, are manually modified with no guarantee of improvement. Learn how SkillOpt turns skill editing into a training process, making agent behavior more reliable without changing model weights.
The post SkillOpt: Agent skills as trainable parameters appeared first on Microsoft Research.
news.summary: Microsoft Research's SkillOpt enables skill editing as a training process for AI agents, making their behavior more reliable without modifying model weights. This is achieved by transforming instruction editing into a training operation.
news.enterprise_use: Check your current workflow for manual AI agent instruction modifications and consider applying analogous techniques from SkillOpt to improve reliability. Inaction means relying on potentially error-prone manual edits, leading to suboptimal AI agent performance.

news.title: Memora: A Harmonic Memory Representation Balancing Abstraction and Specificity
news.summary_raw:
AI agents can't remember past conversations. They must constantly reload or retrieve context, which grows less efficient as tasks get longer and more complex. Memora solves this with a scalable memory system separating what’s stored from how it's retrieved.
The post Memora: A Harmonic Memory Representation Balancing Abstraction and Specificity appeared first on Microsoft Research.
news.summary: Microsoft Research has developed Memora, a harmonious memory representation that balances abstraction and specificity. This allows AI agents to efficiently access past conversations, mitigating the need for constant reloading or context retrieval.
